_about: THE PAYOUT PIPELINE's numbers for THE SET (the owner, 2026-10-13; docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-payout-pipeline-design.md). One idea is asked by templates/pipeline_payout.json; everything here is asked of the set of strategies that trade the funded accounts together. FIRST VERSION: every number is a first setting, the owner's to change, here and nowhere else. Read by blueprint/pay_rules.py.
_slots: The owner's three sessions, New York time: ONE strategy a slot, flat before the next. A trade counts for a slot only when it is entered AND closed inside it; `pool.in_slot` = the share of an idea's trades that must do so for the idea to be a member of that slot (the rest of its trades are left out of every number).
_score: THE MAIN SCORE = the expected payout a week across the accounts over `days` session days (12 weeks), with `short_days` (4 weeks) beside it. Days are drawn in runs of `block` session days so that winning and losing streaks stay together. `request` "max" = a payout is asked for when the MAXIMUM payout can be had (the owner: "max payouts"); "min" = as soon as any payout can. `max_bust` = SURVIVAL: a size and day rule may be chosen only when the account is lost in at most this share of the futures over `days` (the owner: "both are important speed and survival", "its okay if some blow as long as in the end we are in profit"); without it the most paid is always the biggest gamble. A first setting: his to change.
_sizes: The size steps, in micros FOR EACH strategy of the set (one trades at a time: a slot is flat before the next). A step above what the funded account may trade from its first day (its contract limit, or the size its scaling plan starts at) is left out for that account.
_day_rule: After a slot ends, the later slots of that day do not trade once the day is up by `gain` or down by `loss`, each a share of the account's drawdown (null = always trade). The owner: whichever performs best. A setting counts with its neighbours.
_rotation: THE FIXED RULE (the owner took the recommendation 2026-10-13): a strategy is in form when its own equity made a `lookback`-day high within the last `within` session days. Each slot keeps `bench` reserves; each evening the first one in form trades the next day, none in form = the slot stands down. The rule is kept only if it beats no rule on the build days with its neighbours.
_proof: A set is PROVEN when, on the unseen days (each member's ONE read, never used to choose it), its expected payout a week is above $0 and at least `keep` of what it was on the build days.
_firms: `trader_share` = the trader's part of a payout (Lucid 90/10; Apex 100 % of the first $25,000). Apex funded accounts (research/prop-portfolio/2026-10-01-l2/APEX300_RULES.md, Apex's help centre read 2026-10-01): `one_side` = no entry rule that rests orders on both sides; `min_target_r` = the stop may be at most 5x the target, so a box needs a target of 0.2 R or more (a box with no target cannot go on). Every Apex account runs THE SAME set, so two of them are never on opposite sides. NOT in any number here: Apex's ban on automated trading on funded accounts (the owner's decision), its 30 % open-loss rule, half size until the safety net.
_after_payout: What the app's rule files do not say because they simulate the first payout only, by the start of the rule file's id. Lucid Pro: later payouts at most $2,500. Lucid Flex: five payouts, then the account leaves. Apex Legacy: payouts 1-5 at the cap, none from the 6th; from the 4th the balance that must stay is the drawdown + $100 (the conservative reading). After any payout the cycle starts again (winning days, traded days, largest day, cycle profit) and the floor is the locked one.
_accounts: The rule file an account is scored on when the owner has not said: a Lucid account = the pipeline's own account (pipeline.json prop.account), an Apex funded account = the newest Apex Legacy file of its size. <pipeline root>/payout/accounts.json holds the accounts; its `rules` and `on` are the owner's to change.
